Part II - (Presentation Title)¶

Alankrit Agarwal¶

Investigation Overview¶

The overall goal of this presentation is to showcase the riding characteristics of the Ford GoBike system users, specifically highlighting how User Type (Subscriber vs Customer) and Rider Age impact the duration of a bike trip.

Dataset Overview and Executive Summary¶

The dataset includes information regarding individual rides made in a bike-sharing system in the San Francisco Bay area. The data was cleaned to remove missing values and extreme outliers (trips over 1 hour, and riders over 80 years old were excluded).

Key Insights:

  1. Bike share users primarily use the service for very short trips (under 15 minutes).
  2. Casual "Customers" take significantly longer rides on average than annual "Subscribers".
  3. While younger riders show a wide variance in trip durations, older riders adhere almost exclusively to short trips.

# import all packages and set plots to be embedded inline
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# suppress warnings from final output
%matplotlib inline
import warnings
warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
In [2]:
def plot_label(title, x_label, y_label):
    plt.title(title, fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')
    plt.xlabel(x_label, fontsize=12)
    plt.ylabel(y_label, fontsize=12)

# Load and clean data (Executive Summary Data)
df = pd.read_csv('fordgobike.csv')
df = df.dropna()
df['member_age'] = 2019 - df['member_birth_year']
df['member_age'] = df['member_age'].astype(int)
df = df.query('member_age <= 80 and duration_sec <= 3600')
df['user_type'] = df['user_type'].astype('category')

Most Bike Trips are Short Commutes¶

The distribution of trip durations is heavily right-skewed. The massive peak at the beginning of the chart indicates that the core utility of the GoBike system is quick, short-distance commutes rather than long-term rentals.

In [3]:
plt.figure(figsize=[12, 6])
bins = np.arange(0, df['duration_sec'].max()+60, 60)
plt.hist(data=df, x='duration_sec', bins=bins, color='#3498db', edgecolor='black')
plot_label('Distribution of Trip Durations (Under 1 Hour)', 'Trip Duration (Seconds)', 'Total Number of Trips')
plt.show()

Casual Customers Take Longer Rides Than Subscribers¶

Despite subscribers making up the vast majority of total trips, casual customers have a notably higher median trip duration. This suggests subscribers use the bikes for highly efficient daily commuting, while customers may use them for leisure or tourism.

In [4]:
plt.figure(figsize=[12, 6])
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='user_type', y='duration_sec', palette='Set2')
plot_label('Trip Duration Segmented by User Type', 'Type of User', 'Trip Duration (Seconds)')
plt.show()

Rider Age Creates a Natural Ceiling on Duration¶

This multivariate plot combines our findings. The darker dots (Customers) sit systematically higher on the duration axis. Furthermore, a natural barrier forms as age increases; riders over the age of 60 rarely take trips exceeding 2,000 seconds, whereas younger riders show a massive variance in ride lengths.

In [5]:
plt.figure(figsize=[14, 7])
# Using stripplot to prevent the overplotting of discrete integer data (age)
sns.stripplot(data=df, x='member_age', y='duration_sec', hue='user_type', 
              size=2.5, jitter=0.35, dodge=True, palette='viridis', alpha=0.6)

plot_label('Rider Age vs. Trip Duration Segmented by User Type', 'Rider Age (Years)', 'Trip Duration (Seconds)')

# Format X-axis to prevent label overlap
pos, lab = plt.xticks()
plt.xticks(pos[::2], lab[::2])

# Enlarge legend markers
plt.legend(title='User Type', markerscale=4, title_fontsize='12', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Conclusion¶

Through exploratory and explanatory data analysis, it is clear that the Ford GoBike system is predominantly utilized by younger, subscribed users for highly efficient, short-duration commutes. However, significant variances in trip duration are driven primarily by casual customers and users under the age of forty.
